transcript: seeing this musical performed in an actual cemetery honestly gave me so much hope Ghost Quartet is a delightfully strange piece of musical theatre by Dave Malloy the writer behind Natasha Pierre and the Great Comet of 1812 and this revival featuring all four of the original performers was done outdoors in Greenwood Cemetery following a free whiskey tasting for every audience member I was lucky enough to see the very first run of Ghost Quartet back in 2014 at Bushwick Starr and I can't tell you how meaningful it was to return to this piece all these years later and to see how the fan base had grown this experience was honestly like a comic con for fans of alternative musical theatre just this large gathering of weirdos (and of course I'm including myself in that) just all obsessed with this same niche thing and eager to brave the elements to experience it together in this uniquely immersive environment speaking of braving the elements I was actually supposed to see this the night before but the show was cancelled due to lightning risk but they let us stick around and drink whiskey and then they treated us to an impromptu parking lot performance of several of the songs and of course I'm glad I then got to see the real show but this parking lot performance was almost as special because it just showcased this mighty little community surrounding this work Dave Malloy is my favorite living musical theatre composer and I'm genuinely not just saying that because I got to work with him once what?? I've been gatekeeping this story but it's a lore drop for another time but between this the witches album release the upcoming Black Swan musical the production of Octet in Hudson Valley it just feels like a great time to be a Dave Malloy fan which is encouraging for me because I do sometimes feel alone in my very weird specific taste in musical theatre and this experience reminded me that I'm very much not in fact the Dave Malloy Revolution is in full swing and I hope you're all ready for it
